Ivy L: Heads-up 10min design review: compact autoscale row for pool list. Focus: min/max inline editing, SLO slider snap behavior, and revised burst confirmation copy. Also need accessibility checklist. Marco D: Inline editing should allow direct typing and arrow +/- to nudge. If user types value and presses Enter, we save immediately; Esc cancels. Important for keyboard-first flows. Ken (FE): Implementation plan: use contenteditable fallback or numeric input with aria-live region. My preference: numeric input with spin buttons hidden visually, visible up/down steppers for touch. Arrow keys change by step attribute. Priya S: For min/max labels: change to "Minimum instances" and "Maximum instances" (full words) vs shorthand. Users confused by MIN/MAX in testing. Also add small helper text: "Limits autoscale capacity for this route". Ava (a11y): A few a11y bullets: 1) each inline input must have an associated label (visually hidden OK). 2) keyboard users need a way to hold modifier (shift) for larger increments (e.g., shift+arrow = +10). 3) notify screen readers when autoscale config changes via aria-live polite region. Ivy L: Good. On the SLO slider: current prototype snaps to 5% increments. Some PMs want snap to preset buckets (50, 75, 95) plus a fine-grained mode. Thoughts? Marco D: Preset buckets are helpful for onboarding. UX: show small clickable chips under slider: 50%, 75%, 95%. Clicking sets slider. Fine mode toggle reveals a numeric input or switches step to 1%. Ken (FE): Chips + slider is doable. Concern: adding chips reduces space in compact row. Maybe collapse chips behind a chevron popover labeled "presets". Priya S: If chips are hidden, ensure discoverability. Copy for popover: "Common SLOs" with a tooltip. Keep chip labels short. Ava (a11y): Popover must be accessible: focus trap within, close on Esc, and return focus to the triggering control. Provide aria-expanded on the trigger. Ivy L: Burst confirmation language debate: current copy "Enable burst to allocate extra GPUs" is too vague. Need to communicate capacity, max duration, and billing. Proposals: Priya S: Option A: "Enable burst: +{n} GPUs for up to {t} minutes. Billed while active." Option B (more gentle): "Allow temporary capacity boost (+{n} GPUs). We'll auto-revert after {t} minutes unless you extend. Billing applies while burst is active." Which is clearer? Marco D: I prefer B since it mentions auto-revert. Also include a secondary line: "Estimated cost: ~$X/hour" if we can calculate. Ken (FE): UI should show the estimated cost inline and link to detailed billing. CTA should be explicit: "Enable burst (+4 GPUs, 30m)". Cancel button remains "Don't enable" not just "Cancel". Ava (a11y): Modal requirements: 1) trap focus, 2) close on Esc, 3) primary CTA focused by default, 4) aria-describedby for the billing explanation. Also ensure the cost estimate has role=status so it's announced. Ivy L: Pool picker: propose showing unavailable pools disabled with a short reason and an action link "Request access" if possible. Priya S: Microcopy for disabled reason: "Unavailable: reserved by org policy" or "Unavailable: quota reached". Request access link should open a lightweight modal to file a request. Marco D: Backend note: we already return a reason code in the pool list API. UI should render reason text and if requestable=true show the link. No new API work. Ken (FE): Visual treatment: disabled option with 50% opacity, small info icon with tooltip on hover. On selection attempt show role=alert message: "This pool is not available for this project." Ava (a11y): When pool selection changes programmatically (e.g., autoswitch due to policy), fire a live region announcement: "Pool changed to X. Reason: Y." Also ensure color contrast for badges (preemptible/warning) meets AA. Ivy L: Small copy asks: what should the preemptible badge say? "Preemptible" feels technical. Alternatives: "Spot instances (may be interrupted)" or badge plus tooltip. Priya S: I like "Spot (may be interrupted)" — clearer for non-ops users. Tooltip: "Spot/Preemptible instances can be reclaimed; for strict SLOs choose a dedicated pool." Marco D: UX edge-case: what if min>max typed by user? Show inline validation: "Minimum cannot exceed maximum" and prevent save. Also show suggested fix button "Set max to X". Ken (FE): We'll add client-side validation and a small inline button that sets the other field. Keyboard accessible. Ivy L: Final: action items. Ken 10 implement numeric input + steppers and popover for presets (prototype by Tue). Ava 10 supply full a11y checklist and example markup (including aria-live regions and role=status usage). Marco 10 verify API reason codes and cost estimate availability. Priya 10 finalize all microcopy variants and provide a single copy file. Ken (FE): Ack. I'll include examples of the primary CTA label as suggested. Ava (a11y): Quick sample for aria-live region:
Autoscale settings saved

. deploy-bot: Prototype branch pushed: github.com/redwood/autoscale/ui-prototype (ken/numeric-presets) :rocket: Ivy L: Thanks everyone. I'll pull the prototype into the next design pass and run a quick 1:1 with accessibility to verify flow. Closing thread after review.
